acceptance_items: the three frozen Session writes (permission.reply, session.cancel and the dedicated Session body ingress) perform one durable CAS write instead of refusing UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION, and the result reports only the accepted revision and never a Session state
an undeclared agentId is refused typed FORBIDDEN before any write, so the record path is never guessed
session.create and session.open stay typed UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION, because both must return real engine data and a one-way record cannot carry a response

the record has exactly one CAS fence: a stale expectation is REVISION_CONFLICT with the bytes untouched, a failed rename is uncertain with a real fence, and a malformed record is a typed throw never silently repaired
the reader keeps its own consumed watermark in its own data directory and reports the honest behind refusal instead of skipping a write the window already dropped
the watch applies in revision order and stops at the first write it cannot apply, so order is preserved and no write is silently skipped
permission.reply reaches the engine as a JSON-RPC response to the engine's own pending callback and selects only an optionId the engine really offered
the Console body reaches the engine verbatim as session/prompt, and session.cancel makes the daemon's own prompt end with stopReason cancelled
gaps: the control daemon still reports sessions: [] and notifications: [], so the Console sees neither the Session it writes to nor a permission identity from the projection; that projection is L10 and is not delivered here
session.create and session.open stay typed UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION and are deliberately not delivered

source-tree evidence only: the black box starts from the source CLI entry (the worktree generated/runtime-lib), not from an installed artifact, and there is no restart, deployed-entrypoint, cross-device or multi-account receipt
the engine is a local OpenAI-compatible stub provider, not an upstream model, so this proves that the write really reaches and is accepted by an engine, not any model quality

resolved_defects.id: A1 watermark re-apply duplicates a Session body
resolved_defects.found_by: independent review attempt (attack A1), verified and fixed by the unit owner
resolved_defects.defect: A failed watermark save (or a crash) re-applied the same session.message on the next poll, so the engine received a second session/prompt and the Console user saw a duplicated message. The old code comment claimed the apply path refuses an already-satisfied write, which is true only for permission.reply, because that callback is consumed.
fix: an in-process high-water mark appliedThrough; base = max(durableWatermark, appliedThrough ?? 0), so a write already applied in this process is never re-applied
the watermark now saves appliedThrough ?? base, so a partial pass is also durable and the durable watermark never lags a write that already reached the engine
a store fault on the watermark save now maps through configFault like the record-read fault, instead of being flattened to ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE, which wrongly blamed the engine
the apply() comment now says true means the write really reached the engine
resolved_defects.red_green: runtime/session-intent-watch.spec.ts 'never re-applies a write it already applied when the watermark cannot be saved' uses chflags uchg so the watermark reads as 0 but cannot be written. Reverting base to the durable watermark alone makes it fail with host.received length 2 instead of 1, and setting appliedThrough = base also makes it fail; restored, the file is byte-identical and the spec is 12/12.
resolved_defects.residual_boundary: After a crash or restart, writes after the last saved watermark are still applied at least once, so a session.message can still repeat inside that window. This is the at-least-once boundary of this record shape and exactly-once is not claimed.
